avoid: Treating E’s or D’s raw benchmark scores as evidence of discovery success despite zero fresh hits and zero discriminant improvements.
Claiming that S validates every family in its portfolio; the aggregate result provides no lane attribution.
Claiming B or C failed algebraically when they were pruned before benchmark evaluation.
Scaling the entire S portfolio uniformly without measuring each lane’s verified yield, runtime, marginal novelty, and discriminant contribution.
Reusing the previous generation’s A-centered diagnosis or its incompatible 4/83/56 metrics.
Inferring hidden seeds, missing-pair identities, or group signatures from the aggregate counts.
generation_feedback.diagnosis: S was the generation’s only measured success: it found 1 fresh missing pair on 1 fresh seed and produced 4 discriminant improvements, earning acceptance. This supports the operational value of its protected, deterministically scheduled portfolio, but the aggregate metrics do not identify which construction lane produced the novelty or improvements. A’s tower ablation was fully benchmarked and found no fresh pairs or discriminant improvements, so the proposed concentration of effort did not reproduce the prior generation’s tower gains. D likewise produced no measured novelty or record improvements, while E’s high raw scores also translated into zero discovery metrics. B and C were screen-pruned and remain untested rather than algebraically refuted. The supplied previous feedback refers to incompatible outcomes and should not be reused for this generation.
generation_feedback.next_generation_direction: Use S as the backbone, but instrument a deterministic leave-one-lane-out and quota-matched ablation of its tower, preimage-tree, relative-quartic, reciprocal, square-discriminant, and Eisenstein lanes. Record per-lane verified outputs, marginal fresh hits after global deduplication, seed reach, discriminant improvements, and runtime; then retain the smallest complementary mixture that reproduces S’s discovery while preserving a separately capped record-refinement quota.
what_worked: S combined one fresh discovery with 4 discriminant improvements, the strongest relevant result in the generation.
Protected family quotas and deterministic weighted scheduling plausibly preserved complementary search lanes, although lane-level attribution was not recorded.
S demonstrated that discovery and record refinement can coexist when discriminant minimization remains a late, within-cell tie-break.
